minutes.headline: School Committee votes to hand the Kids Kingdom playground back to the town for good.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a proposal for no-cost EV charging stations, got an update on the track/turf field capital project and its engineering study, and voted to remit Kids Kingdom playground to the town. It also covered a midyear curriculum report, the 2026-27 calendar, an FY26 budget update showing on-track spending, and next steps on Turkey Hill accessibility and MSBA planning ahead of an expected override.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to permanently return the Kids Kingdom playground to town control.
After an update on the track/turf field project, the committee agreed to ask the superintendent to request a placeholder warrant article for the engineering funding.
A member was tasked with drafting a framework for deciding between rebuilding Turkey Hill or building new under MSBA before that choice comes back for a vote.
The committee said it wants to align with the select board and finance committee on one override figure at the next tri-board meeting.
The business manager reported FY26 spending on track, running slightly ahead of the same point last year.

why_it_matters: Returning Kids Kingdom shifts upkeep and liability for that playground from the school district to the town.
A placeholder warrant article for the track/field project, and a coming decision on rebuilding versus replacing Turkey Hill, are steps toward items that could appear on a town ballot.
The push for one shared override number across the three boards signals that residents may be asked to vote on a single town-wide tax increase rather than separate asks.
watch_next: The next tri-board meeting, where the boards aim to settle on one override figure
A future school committee vote on Tony's rebuild-vs-new framework for Turkey Hill

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every substantive fact where both actually state one — the Kids Kingdom outcome, the $3.267M capital total, the ~$200K field study, the $30 blankets, the $15–20 Great Wolf fundraiser, the $1,250,000 Turkey Hill accessibility estimate, and Tony's THES framework assignment — but the official minutes are a condensed narrative that drops nearly every dollar figure, percentage, and specific directive our captioned minutes captured, and it records the curriculum-report vote (which our recording could not make out) while omitting the Kids Kingdom vote tally's context and several attendees present in the room. The single item a reader should actually check is the curriculum-report motion, since our minutes could not confirm it passed at all and the official minutes say it did unanimously.
